title: indigo_agent_scheduler: avoid meridian flips in the best visibility plan with a flip penalty
description:
Owner request (2026-11-20): make the best-visibility (VISIBILITY) plan avoid meridian flips when that costs little observing quality, especially for short tasks. Agreed design:

1. Input. The meridian flip is a global mount/telescope setting made at startup (enable_meridian_flip() in a startup script), published by Sequencer.js as Scripting Agent MERIDIAN_FLIP (ENABLED 0|1, USE_SOLVER, OFFSET h in -2..2; tickets 5e7ef4f3, a3ef4543). Task scripts do not set it and SCHEDULER_ESTIMATE / Sequence.estimate() are NOT changed: whether a run flips depends on where it is placed, so the planner decides it per placement. observe_property() caches ENABLED/OFFSET/USE_SOLVER in observed (under observed->mutex) on define/update and bumps a flip generation when a value changes; delete of the property or device = disabled; before the first update = disabled. process() sets plan_dirty when the generation differs from the last plan's. update_plan() copies the cached values once; planning never reads properties. The plan assumes the values do not change during the night.

2. Real flip behaviour (verified in code): the Imager Agent pauses the batch before the first exposure that would end past HA = OFFSET (time_to_transit <= exposure - PAUSE_AFTER_TRANSIT, indigo_agent_imager.c ~1349, once per batch); the flipper waits for Mount Agent FLIP_REQUIRED (TIME_TO_TRANSIT <= 0, i.e. HA >= 0, indigo_agent_mount.c ~1152), then slews, optionally recentres, restarts guiding and settles. A run started past transit (HA >= 0) is slewed to the west side and does not flip. So a run flips iff HA_start < 0 and HA reaches OFFSET before the run ends. With OFFSET < 0 the capture also idles from max(HA_start, OFFSET) until HA = 0.

3. Flip check (indigo_agent_scheduler_plan.c), replacing the prototype (scratchpad flip/plan_flip.diff, which used globals): indigo_scheduler_flip_loss(sky, target, header, start, duration, flip) returns 0 when there is no flip (flip disabled, no target, invalid grids, HA_start >= 0, or HA_start + duration * sidereal rate < OFFSET), else the penalty hours plus, for OFFSET < 0, the wait -max(HA_start, OFFSET) h. HA_start from target->hour_angle[] advanced at the sidereal rate, normalised to [-12, 12). Exposure granularity ignored.

4. Cost in the objective: in vis_table() value[i][g] -= 100 * flip_loss (lost hours valued as full-quality imaging), not for urgent runs. The COMPACT value VISIBILITY compares itself with (info->compact_value) gets the same cost; the COMPACT plan itself is unchanged. Pins and the previous-plan seed use the same table.

5. Durations stay fixed (the plan code assumes a fixed length per task); flip time is not added to the run duration. Possible later addition.

6. Setting: new AGENT_SCHEDULER_SETTINGS number item VISIBILITY_FLIP_PENALTY (name in indigo_names.h AGENT_SCHEDULER_SETTINGS_VISIBILITY_FLIP_PENALTY_ITEM_NAME), label "Best visibility: meridian flip penalty (min)", 0..120 step 1, default 10, placed right after ALTITUDE_WEIGHT. Meaning: minutes of best-quality imaging the user is willing to give up to avoid one flip (at least the time a flip takes; higher avoids flips more strongly; 0 = off). It must be clearly stated everywhere that it is best-visibility only: ignored under COMPACT, no effect while MERIDIAN_FLIP.ENABLED is 0 or the property is missing. A change replans. indigo_scheduler_plan_visibility() gets a const scheduler_flip *flip parameter (enabled, offset h, penalty h; NULL = none); update the agent, unit tests, indigo_test/benchmark/bench_scheduler_plan.c and check tools/scheduler_sandbox.py.

7. The published plan marks runs that will flip.

Study (5000 simulated nights, OFFSET 0): COMPACT 645 flips, 69.7 % time-weighted quality; VISIBILITY 1436 flips, 79.6 %; VISIBILITY + penalty 10 min 269 flips (-81 %), 78.9 %, runs unchanged (5879); penalty 20: 141 flips, 78.5 %. Penalising COMPACT is not worth it (it loses runs).

Tests: unit (test_agent_scheduler_plan.c): flip_loss for OFFSET -, 0, +, starts before/after transit and between a negative offset and transit (wait included), end just short of / past OFFSET; a short crossing task is moved, a long one keeps its flip; urgent runs ignore the cost; penalty 0 or flip disabled gives plans identical to today. Integration (test_agent_scheduler.c, the test Scripting Agent defines MERIDIAN_FLIP): cached, a change replans, an unchanged update does not, delete disables. Benchmark: flips and quality with/without the penalty. Docs: INDIGO_SCHEDULER_GUIDE.md (settings table, the VISIBILITY weights paragraph), doc/SCHEDULER.md, PROPERTIES.md.

outcome.summary: Code matches the approved design and owner answers Q1-Q4: flip_hour_angle/flip_needed/flip_loss (plan.c:114-154; HA from hour_angle[k] + elapsed*1.0027379, normalised to [-12,12), flip iff HA<0 and HA_end>=OFFSET, penalty<=0 returns 0 incl. negative-offset wait), cost in vis_table (plan.c:479-482) and compact_value (plan.c:1139-1142) with urgent exemption; NULL/disabled/penalty 0 subtract exactly 0 so plans are bit-identical (also asserted by visibility_flip_off_is_today). Agent: cache under observed->mutex with generation (scheduler.c:3447-3459), delete of property/device disables (3524-3528), process() marks plan_dirty on generation change (2555-2561), update_plan copies values once (2352-2359), label mark (2246-2247), SETTINGS item 5 with shifted macros and count 11, names.h, DRIVER_VERSION 0x0300001F. Unit test_agent_scheduler_plan all passed; make -C indigo_test test-agent-scheduler 138/138 passed incl. the four new flip cases. Defects: (1) indigo_docs/INDIGO_SCHEDULER_GUIDE.md:254 inserts the heading '#### Meridian flips' in the middle of 'Choosing a strategy', so the worked **Example.** (265), **When to use which.** (279) and **What VISIBILITY respects.** (284) now sit under 'Meridian flips'. Move the subsection after the end of the strategy material (before '### Time windows', line 304) or keep the strategy paragraphs together. (2) The guide's worked example table (265-275) gives the VISIBILITY placement without the flip, while the guide now recommends enabling the flip in the STARTUP hook (Unpark example, 633) and the default penalty is 10; SCHEDULER.md states the penalty removes all three flips of that example. Say in the example that it assumes the meridian flip disabled (or penalty 0). Minor, non-blocking: vis_table's best-start sentinel 'double best = -1' (plan.c:470) predates negative values; with a large penalty a task whose every start flips keeps best_minute -1, which only affects the seed ordering heuristic at plan.c:1189 (use VIS_NONE).

Independent review of master...HEAD (6e83f711e). Flip check (indigo_agent_scheduler_plan.c:115-155): HA from target->hour_angle[k] (grid already normalised to [-12,12)) advanced at 1.00273790935 and renormalised once; flips iff HA_start<0 and HA_start+d*rate>=OFFSET; loss = penalty + (OFFSET<0 ? -max(HA_start,OFFSET) : 0); penalty<=0 returns 0 so the wait is switched off too (Q1). vis_table (:471-483) subtracts 100*loss only for non-urgent runs and now starts best at VIS_NONE, so all-negative tables get a best_minute; the DP/search use VIS_NONE sentinels throughout and handle negative values. compact_value (:1139-1143) gets the same non-urgent cost; plan_order keeps flip NULL. Agent: MERIDIAN_FLIP cached under observed->mutex with offset clamp and generation bump only on change (indigo_agent_scheduler.c:3447-3459), delete of property/device disables (:3524-3528), process() marks plan_dirty on generation change (:2555-2561), update_plan copies values once (:2352-2359); settings change already sets plan_dirty. VISIBILITY_FLIP_PENALTY 0..120 step 1 default 10 after ALTITUDE_WEIGHT, item macros reindexed, count 11; name in indigo_names.h. Label marks flips under both strategies via indigo_scheduler_run_flips, independent of penalty (Q2). DRIVER_VERSION 0x1E->0x1F. Docs: guide Meridian flips subsection now precedes Time windows (293 vs 304), worked example states flip disabled and the F=10 outcome - verified with bench_scheduler_plan owner's night: Soul 21:26, Pleiades 22:22, Jellyfish 00:51, 0 flips, 94.5 %; STARTUP-hook advice consistent across guide (Rules for the body, Hooks Unpark example), SCHEDULER.md and per-task examples; PROPERTIES.md states best-visibility only, COMPACT ignored, ENABLED 0/missing. Previous review items all resolved. Tests run here: build OK; make test-unit exit 0; test_agent_scheduler_plan 41/41 PASS (flips 405 -> 101); make test-agent-scheduler 138 run, 138 passed. history.text: Verifying scheduler code claims against sources
design.md written, 4 open questions for the owner

Owner answers to design.md open questions (2026-11-20): Q1 penalty 0 switches the whole cost off, the negative-offset wait included (plans identical to today). Q2 mark flipping runs under both strategies whenever MERIDIAN_FLIP.ENABLED is 1 (information only under COMPACT). Q3 the label check plus code review is enough, no test-only observable. Q4 yes: the docs (INDIGO_SCHEDULER_GUIDE.md, SCHEDULER.md) recommend setting the meridian flip once in the STARTUP hook, explain that the planner uses the current MERIDIAN_FLIP, and the per-task advice and task examples are adjusted. Correction: the simulation used 1000 random nights, not 5000.
Plan code done; wiring MERIDIAN_FLIP cache, setting and plan mark into the agent
Building library and scheduler archive in the worktree
Running the scheduler plan benchmark (1000 nights)
Writing integration tests for the MERIDIAN_FLIP cache
Running scheduler integration cases filtered on flip
Running the full scheduler integration suite; updating the documentation
Check command-1 started: make -C indigo_test test-agent-scheduler

Benchmark (indigo_test/benchmark/bench_scheduler_plan, 1000 random nights, lat 42 lon 23, 2026-11-19, flip OFFSET 0, flips counted with indigo_scheduler_run_flips on executed runs): COMPACT 5626 runs, 645 flips (0.65/night), weighted quality 69.7 %; VISIBILITY (no penalty) 5879 runs, 1436 flips (1.44/night), 79.6 %; VISIBILITY F=10 (default penalty) 5879 runs, 269 flips (0.27/night, -81 %), 78.9 %. Owner's night: VISIBILITY 3 flips 95.8 % weighted -> F=10 0 flips 94.5 %. No night with fewer runs than COMPACT, 0 violations for all strategies; F=10 has 26 nights with the same runs as COMPACT and a lower raw weighted quality (expected: the comparison with COMPACT now includes flip costs). Plain VISIBILITY plan time p99 27.87 ms, max 38.87 ms. Unit test visibility_flip_never_fewer_runs: 405 -> 101 flips over its 250 random queues. Matches the design's prototype simulation.
Running unit plan test and make test-agent-scheduler in worktree
Implementation resumed: the review requested changes
Fixing review notes: guide section order, example assumption, vis_table best init
Check command-1 started: make -C indigo_test test-agent-scheduler
Running plan unit test and make test-agent-scheduler
